title: Leaky ReLU
body:
$$
\text{LeakyReLU}(z) = \begin{cases} z & z > 0 \\ \alpha z & z \le 0\end{cases}, \qquad
\frac{d}{dz} = \begin{cases} 1 & z > 0 \\ \alpha & z < 0 \end{cases}
$$

[[ReLU]] with a shallow slope instead of a flat floor, typically $\alpha = 0.01$. **It exists for
exactly one reason: to fix dead units.** ReLU's derivative is $0$ for negative $z$, so a unit
pushed there receives no gradient and can never recover. Here the derivative is $\alpha$, small but
non-zero, so the unit keeps getting a signal and can climb back out.

Everything else about [[ReLU]] carries over unchanged: still [[Non-Linear]] (the kink is still
there), still cheap, still derivative $1$ on the positive side so gradients do not vanish with
depth. What it gives up is sparsity, since nothing outputs exactly zero any more.

$\alpha$ is a hyperparameter. The variant that learns it per unit instead of fixing it is called
PReLU, which the vault has no note for.

**When to reach for it:** not by default. Use [[ReLU]], and switch if a large fraction of a layer
has gone permanently silent. The gain is usually small, which is why plain ReLU is still the
standard answer.
